comments.content: On the final permitted iteration (`step == self.max_steps`) the tool calls are still executed and their results appended to `messages`, but the loop then falls through and returns `AgentError::MaxStepsExceeded`, so the transcript and the (possibly side-effecting) tool outputs are discarded and the model never gets to produce a final answer. Consider not executing tools on the last step (the run is already guaranteed to fail), or returning the partial transcript alongside the error so callers can inspect what happened.

comments.content: The assistant message is copied twice per step: `assistant.tool_calls.clone()` copies the tool-call vector, then `messages.push(assistant.clone())` copies the whole message (including those same tool calls). Since `assistant` is only needed again for the no-tool-call success branch, you can take the calls out first (declare `assistant` as `mut`, use `assistant.tool_calls.take().unwrap_or_default()`) and then push `assistant.clone()` once, cutting the duplication from two clones to one.

comments.content: `enable_thinking` is hardcoded to `Some(true)` while every other generation option (temperature, timeout, max_steps, model) is sourced from `Config`. The CLI already exposes `--think`/`--no-think`, so once this loop is wired in the flag would be silently ignored. Consider adding a thinking field to `Config` and reading it here for consistency.

comments.content: There is no bound on the number of tool calls executed per step and no timeout around each `execute` call; `ToolRegistry::execute` enforces no per-call timeout either. A model returning many calls, or a tool that blocks (e.g. slow filesystem), can stall the run sequentially for an unbounded time. Consider bounding the tool-call count and/or wrapping execution in a timeout.

comments.content: The tests only exercise the trivial no-tool path and input validation. The central behavior of this module — the multi-step tool-calling loop and the max-steps guard — has no coverage at all, which is exactly why the transcript-discarding bug on the final step slipped through. Consider adding: (1) a test where the model first returns `tool_calls` and the registry executes the tool, then the next model response returns a final message, asserting the transcript is `user → assistant(tool_calls) → tool → assistant`; and (2) a test where the model keeps returning tool calls until `max_steps`, asserting `AgentError::MaxStepsExceeded`.
